description: Prompts that rank candidate snippets by how likely they show a pedestrian problem. A window scores by how much a group's best prompt beats the best routine-scene prompt on the same keyframes. They only rank windows for the VLMs; they decide nothing about the scene. British English throughout.

pavement_condition: a street with no pavement where people have to walk in the road
a broken, cracked or uneven pavement beside the road
a pavement too narrow for two people to walk side by side
pavement_obstruction: cars parked on the pavement blocking pedestrians
street stalls, bins or poles blocking the pavement
roadworks or construction closing the pavement
crossing_facilities: a busy wide road with no pedestrian crossing
a faded or missing zebra crossing at a junction
a large junction where pedestrians have no signal or refuge island
pedestrian_exposure: pedestrians walking in the carriageway next to moving traffic
people crossing the road between moving cars
pedestrians waiting in the middle of the road to cross busy traffic
accessibility: a high kerb with no dropped kerb or ramp at a crossing
steps or barriers on the footway that block wheelchair users
a person with a pushchair or wheelchair struggling along the street
vulnerable_users: children or elderly people walking close to fast traffic
a crowded street where people spill into the road
a market or school area with many pedestrians beside traffic

negative_prompts: an empty motorway with no pedestrians or buildings
a road through countryside with no people and no pavements
the inside of a road tunnel
a tidy street with wide clear pavements and marked crossings
the inside of a car park or garage
a car dashboard or interior filling the view
